reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to confirm EGFR engagement by erlotinib. The trial provides no PD/PK readout bearing on target binding. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to assess whether EGFR inhibition led to downstream signaling changes. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (PFS) clearly failed - erlotinib arm had median PFS of 1.91 months vs 3.52 months for standard chemotherapy, showing erlotinib was inferior to control. Response rate was also lower (2/52 vs 6/51 PR). 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No biomarker-defined subgroups analyzed. The enrolled population was advanced NSCLC patients with ECOG PS 2, but no evidence this was the wrong population for EGFR inhibition. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Adequate sample size (103 patients), reasonable treatment duration (21.7 weeks), no major safety issues preventing dosing. This appears to be a clean efficacy failure rather than a trial design issue.
